title: Marathon: no speargun use in any manmade canal
effect: Inside the City of Marathon it is unlawful to use, fire or discharge a speargun on or below the surface of any manmade canal; the speargun is forfeited on conviction.
excerpt: Prohibited activity. It is unlawful for any person to use, fire or discharge any speargun, as defined above, on or below the surface of any manmade canal.
full: Definition. A speargun is any device, whether commercially manufactured or handmade, which is so designed and constructed so as to be capable of forcefully discharging at great velocity any spear or any similar projectile in a direction determined by the user thereof for a distance greater than two (2) feet (24 inches), whether or not such spear or projectile is tethered to the firing apparatus or otherwise limited in its range. No distinction shall be made as to the mechanical construction or physical means utilized in such devices to create the potential energy necessary to eject or fire such spear or similar projectiles. Prohibited activity. It is unlawful for any person to use, fire or discharge any speargun, as defined above, on or below the surface of any manmade canal. Penalties. Any person convicted of a violation of this section shall be penalized in accordance with Section 1-7. In addition, any person convicted of a violation of this section shall forfeit the speargun used by such person in committing such offense to the City for destruction in the same manner as forfeited firearms are disposed of by the Sheriff. (Code 1999, § 13-5)
scope: All manmade canals within the City of Marathon city limits (Monroe County). The section names no canal list or map.
note: Checked 30 Sep 2026: read in Chrome on the city's own code site (Marathon has left Municode; library.municode.com/fl/marathon redirects to marathon.municipalcodeonline.com). Supersedes the secondary entry marathon-canal (keyssao.org flyer) as the authority for the Marathon canal closure; keep marathon-canal only if the unincorporated Monroe County half of the flyer still needs it (see monroe-26-art4). Geometry: no canal layer is named in the law; draw from a canal dataset only with a flag, or mark as a text-only rule.

title: Town of Palm Beach: no spearfishing gear on five named public beaches
effect: Possession of spearfishing equipment is banned on Phipps Ocean Park, Midtown Beach, the Clarke Avenue beach, the Kreusler Park beach and the Palm Beach Inlet dock; on other Town beaches a speargun must be carried uncocked and unloaded.
excerpt: The possession of spearfishing equipment is prohibited and declared to be unlawful on those areas of the public beach within the town specifically designated by the town for public use described as follows:
full: (b) Prohibited. The possession of spearfishing equipment is prohibited and declared to be unlawful on those areas of the public beach within the town specifically designated by the town for public use described as follows: (1) Phipps Ocean Park, consisting of approximately 1,200 linear feet adjacent to the waters of the Atlantic Ocean. (2) Midtown Beach, beginning at an area 150 feet north of Royal Palm Way, south to Gulfstream Road. (3) The Clarke Avenue Beach area from Barton Avenue on the north to Sea Breeze Avenue on the south. (4) The public beach known as Kreusler Park running north of the City of Lake Worth casino property extending approximately 500 feet northerly therefrom. (5) The Inlet Dock facility located at the Palm Beach Inlet (Lake Worth Inlet). (c) Regulated. On those areas of the public beach not described above, spearfishing equipment shall be carried in a manner so as to keep the equipment from being accidentally or intentionally discharged and shall be carried in a manner so as not to be cocked, loaded, engaged or aimed. Definitions in (a): 'Beaches means that area abutting the Atlantic Ocean or Lake Worth consisting of predominately sand, whether below or above the mean high water mark. Spearfishing equipment means any spear, gig or lance intended for use of spearfishing and which is propelled by rubber bands, metal springs, or the explosion or expansion of powder, gas, or similar substance.' (Code 1982, § 14-33; Ord. No. 15-95, § 2, 9-12-95)
scope: Town of Palm Beach public beaches listed in (b)(1) to (5); (c) applies on all other Town public beach. 'Beaches' includes sand below mean high water.
note: Checked 30 Sep 2026: NEW, found by whole-code Municode search (client 9332). A possession rule on the beach, not a water closure, but it blocks shore entry with a speargun at the named beaches. Distinct from the Palm Beach County refuges (pbc-13-55). Geometry: beach segments are described by street names; do not draw without a street/parcel source.

title: Town of Palm Beach: diving off guarded beaches needs a buddy, cert card, BC and flag
effect: Skin or scuba diving off lifeguarded Town beaches is unlawful unless divers use the buddy system, scuba divers carry a certification card, each diver has a BC, and each dive unit flies a dive flag.
excerpt: It shall be unlawful to skin or scuba dive off public beaches operated and patrolled and guarded by lifeguards of the town unless adequate safety precautions are taken.
full: It shall be unlawful to skin or scuba dive off public beaches operated and patrolled and guarded by lifeguards of the town unless adequate safety precautions are taken. (1) The "buddy" system must be used, making it necessary to have two or more people diving. It shall be unlawful to dive alone. (2) If scuba diving, each member must have a current nationally recognized open water certification card. (3) Each diver must have a buoyancy compensator capable of supporting the head of an unconscious diver above the water. (4) Each dive unit must have a diver's down flag. This flag must be free flying and clearly visible to boaters from a minimum of 100 feet in all directions. The flag must be a minimum of 12 inches by 12 inches and must have a red diagonal background with a white stripe. An international alpha flag may be used in lieu of the above flag. (Code 1982, § 14-64)
scope: Off Town of Palm Beach public beaches that are lifeguarded.
note: Checked 30 Sep 2026: NEW. A condition, not a closure; render as a text note on the guarded beaches.

title: Pompano Beach: no swimming or diving in the Hillsboro Inlet area
effect: Swimming or diving of any kind is unlawful in city waters of the Hillsboro Inlet area described in § 91.22(A), except commercial or governmental diving authorised in writing by the City Manager.
excerpt: (A) It shall be unlawful for any person to swim or in any manner dive in any waters of the city located within the following area.
full: (A) ... Beginning at the intersection of the Hillsboro Inlet and the easterly boundary of the State of Florida; then northwesterly along the center line of Hillsboro Inlet and the center line of Hillsboro Bay, to an intersection with the center line of the Intracoastal Waterway from Jacksonville, Florida, to Miami, Florida; then southwesterly along the center line of the Intracoastal Waterway, to a point of intersection with a projection of the westerly boundary of lot 19, block 20, Hillsboro Shores, section B, according to the plat thereof recorded in plat book 2, page 39, of the public record of Broward County, Florida; then southerly along the projection of the westerly lot line of the aforesaid lot 19 to a point of intersection with the north lot line of lot 19; then easterly and northeasterly along the north line of block 20, section B, Hillsboro Shores, to a point of intersection with the north boundary of Section 29, Township 48 South, Range 43 east; then easterly along the aforesaid section line to a point of intersection with the easterly lot line of lot 27, block 20, Hillsboro Shores, section B; then southeasterly along the easterly lot line to the northerly right-of-way line of State Road A-l-A; then southeasterly to a point of intersection with the southerly right-of-way line of State Road A-1-A and the easterly lot line of lot 33, block 10, Hillsboro Shores, section A, according to the plat thereof recorded in plat book 21, page 14, of the public records of Broward County, Florida; then southerly along the easterly lot line to the southerly boundary of the aforesaid block 10; then southwesterly and southerly along the southeasterly and easterly boundary of the aforesaid block 10 to a point of intersection with the south lot line of lot 20, block 10, Hillsboro Shores, section A; then easterly to the point of beginning; the lands situate, lying, and being in the City of Pompano Beach, Broward County, Florida. (B) The City Manager may authorize skindiving, scuba diving, or other similar commercial diving or swimming, not for sport, leisure, or recreation, when it is connected with a bona-fide governmental or similar project in the waters covered hereby. Permission shall be obtained in writing prior to such swimming or diving. ('58 Code, § 6A.12) (Ord. 772, passed 7-10-62) Penalty, see § 10.99
scope: Hillsboro Inlet and Hillsboro Bay centreline from the state's easterly boundary to the ICW, plus Hillsboro Shores sections A and B lots named in the text (City of Pompano Beach). Described in words and plat references only.
note: Checked 30 Sep 2026: boundary read in full in Chrome and string-matched against the page; upgrades the entry from secondary to verbatim. No coordinates in the law; drawing needs Broward parcel GIS for the named lots. The starting point 'the easterly boundary of the State of Florida' is ambiguous (state boundary is 3 nm offshore); conservative reading draws the inlet centreline seaward to it. Hillsboro Inlet also carries the 100 ft jetty buffer in r. 68B-20.003(2)(d).
